source: NAVSHIPS 250-624 (1948), Sec. XI Maintenance Parts Catalog, Figs. 106-110, pp. 78-88; totals checked against Sec. XII, p. 89

relations.round: the part goes round the named part (its bore on a shaft, pipe, post or screw), kinds as in
relations.embed: a thread or pin across a part drawn without a hole for it (an extrusion or turned solid that can't be holed across): inside its metal
relations.in: the part's axis (a screw's thread, an arbor's pivot, a pin, a post, or a ring's outside) inside the named part: tap (thread in a tapped hole), clear (through a clearance hole), run (a pivot in its bearing), free (turning on a post or pipe), press (pressed in)
relations.on: rests against the named part (surfaces within 0.02 mm)
relations.mesh: teeth engage: centre distance m(z1+z2)/2, the same module, the faces overlapping, turning in the tooth ratio
relations.endshake: axial play between the named bearings or endstones, 0.001-0.003 in (Ops. 15, 69, 74)

lines.name: Ship Chronometer Assembly (serials 1-337)

lines.name: Case - Carrying, complete

lines.name: Gimbal Assembly

lines.name: Screw - Case support strap

lines.name: Nut - Pivot screw lock (case rear)

dev.why: The manual has all three upper train bridge screws in pillars (reassembly Op. 14; disassembly Ops. 47, 48). The model's third screw is at (29.24, -12.28), where the top-view photograph shows a screw head sunk in a clearance hole through the barrel bridge (C Spinner's restoration video, 23:30, shows that hole through the bridge laid flat); a pillar there would stand in the fusee wheel, whose size the layout fixes, so it is drawn threaded into the bridge alone (IDEAS.md 1.2). What it holds in the real movement is not settled.
